subject: Request: short-term headroom + overrun escrow for BrightScale launch
messages:
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@brightscale.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightscale.ai, Jake Li <jake.li@brightscale.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Short-term headroom and overrun handling for launch week

Hi Alex / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the throughput looked great. We have a peak launch scheduled for Nov 4 and preliminary traffic forecasts show ~3.5x expected token volume for a 72-hour window. Our procurement team asked whether Redwood can provide a short-term quota uplift and an overrun escrow arrangement so we can avoid blocking traffic while procurement finalizes a PO.

Concretely: can you authorize a temporary headroom (up to 4x committed QPS) for 72 hours starting Nov 3 UTC, and accept overrun charges to be captured to an escrow account (procurement will wire once the PO clears)? We'd also appreciate any one-time launch credits or a marginal rate discount given the committed annual spend we discussed.

I've attached a week-one usage export and a short PO summary for context. Happy to hop on a call if needed.

Thanks,
Emily Chen
Head of Engineering
BrightScale

Attachment: BrightScale_PO_Summary.pdf (summary of planned spend and timelines)
Attachment: usage_report_oct_week1.csv (sample traffic)
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@brightscale.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Oct 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-term headroom and overrun handling for launch week

Emily — really appreciate the heads up and the export, that helps a lot. Short answer: we can support a time-limited uplift and accept overrun charges into an escrow, but I need to coordinate a couple of things internally (billing ops + legal) to lock the exact mechanics.

Next steps I propose:
- I'll provision a provisional headroom pool (provisional QPS uplift) that can be enabled on Nov 3 UTC for a 72-hour window.
- Ben, can you advise on the marginal token rate we can offer for the overrun that enters escrow? We can do a blended rate vs. the pay-as-you-go list to make it cost-predictable for them.
- Marissa / Priyom — can you review the attached PO summary and prepare a one-page amendment draft that defines the escrow acceptance conditions and billing fallback? We want to ensure we don't expose Redwood to unpaid consumption.

If this all looks reasonable I'll confirm by EOD and send an amended order form draft. If procurement wants a call, I'm available 11:30–12:30 PT today.

—Alex
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@brightscale.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Oct 2025 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-term headroom and overrun handling for launch week

Alex / team — thanks for looping me in. Per pricing, we can structure the overrun in one of two ways:

Option A (simple escrow): overrun billed at PayGO list price, purchaser wires amount to escrow within 7 business days of invoice; if payment received we refund any unused escrow balance.

Option B (discounted provisional rate): provide a 12% discount on the marginal overrun token rate in exchange for an authorization to charge up to X tokens to the customer's card on file if escrow isn't funded by T+10 business days. This requires legal signoff for a temporary authorization clause in the amendment.

Given BrightScale's discussed annual commit, I'm inclined to recommend Option B (discount + conditional authorization) to balance their cashflow needs and Redwood's risk. Marissa / Priyom, can you draft language that limits the authorization to the Nov 3–Nov 5 window only and requires two signatories from procurement?

Also: we should be explicit about rate ceilings and a hard throttle threshold to avoid runaway costs. I'll share a suggested marginal rate matrix later today.

—Ben
Director, Revenue Operations
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Chen <emily.chen@brightscale.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Oct 2025 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-term headroom and overrun handling for launch week

Team — drafted a short amendment (see attached name) that includes:
- Scope: temporary uplift window (Nov 3 00:00 UTC — Nov 6 00:00 UTC) up to 4x baseline QPS.
- Escrow flow: BrightScale deposits estimated overrun into escrow (wire instructions included). If escrow not funded by T+3 business days, Redwood may (i) throttle at pre-agreed hard-limit or (ii) invoice immediately and apply Option B conditional authorization only if explicitly signed.
- Authorization clause: limited authorization to charge card only for confirmed unpaid overrun related to the uplift window; capped at the dollar amount equivalent to 150% of estimated overrun.
- Discount: 10% provisional marginal discount if escrow route used; 6% discount if conditional auth is required.

Emily — two asks: please confirm procurement signatory names and whether your payment team can do a same-day wire on Nov 3 (we'll need banking lead time). Ben — happy to tighten wording if you prefer Option B terms.

Attachment: redwood_proposed_amendment_v1.docx

—Marissa
Sr. Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@brightscale.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Oct 2025 15:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-term headroom and overrun handling for launch week

Thanks everyone — the amendment draft looks good and procurement confirmed they can wire to escrow on Nov 3 provided wire instructions are sent by close of business Nov 2. Signatories: Linda Park (Procurement Dir) and Tony Gomez (CFO).

BrightScale accepts the 10% provisional marginal discount tied to escrow funding. If we can't move funds in time, procurement has authorized the conditional card authorization up to the capped amount you described, provided Redwood only uses that as a last resort and notifies us immediately.

Can you send the final amendment and the wire instructions so procurement can queue the transfer? Also, Alex — please confirm when you'll enable the provisional headroom pool so we can run a smoke test before Nov 3.

Appreciate the quick work here — look forward to getting this locked.

—Emily
Head of Engineering, BrightScale
